record.original_question: Does there exist a geproci set in linearly general position, or can one prove that no linearly general geproci set exists?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.8. Find an example of a linearly general geproci set, or show that no such example exists.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A finite set of points $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ is called geproci (short for "general projection complete intersection") if there exist integers $a \le b$ such that the image of $Z$ under projection from a general point $p \in \mathbb{P}^3$ to a plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ is a complete intersection of plane curves of degrees $a$ and $b$ (so in particular $|Z| = ab$).

A finite set $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ is said to be in linearly general position if no $4$ of its points are coplanar (equivalently, every $4$ points of $Z$ span $\mathbb{P}^3$). 

Determine whether there exists a geproci set $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ in linearly general position, or prove that no such set exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent work on geproci-type point configurations in projective space states explicitly that the existence of a geproci set in $\mathbb{P}^3$ in linearly general position is still open. By contrast, in $\mathbb{P}^4$ infinitely many "geprofi" sets in linear general position are known, but this does not resolve the original $\mathbb{P}^3$ question.

status_evidence.title: Finite sets of points in P^4 with special projection properties
status_evidence.snippet: existence of geproci sets in P^3 in LGP ... 'This question is still open' ... by contrast there are infinitely many geprofi sets in P^4 in LGP
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a geproci set in P^3 in linearly general position is explicitly noted as still open.

status_evidence.title: Geproci sets: an instance of a new perspective on classification in algebraic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: families of examples of such sets in P^3 have been constructed and studied; finding non-grid examples is highly non-trivial
status_evidence.claim: Known nontrivial geproci examples in P^3 (e.g., from D4, F4, H4 root systems) are not in linearly general position.
